idx_t INFLOW_MAT_ID = 1;\nconstexpr idx_t OUTFLOW_MAT_ID = 2;\n\n// Build a 2D square grid as an unstructured mesh\n// This represents computation on arbitrarily-shaped geometries\nvoid buildSquare2D(World& world, const int n_elems_root) {\n    const int n_elems = n_elems_root * n_elems_root;\n    \n    // Initialize materials\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.0});    // Default material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.5});    // Inflow material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, -0.5});   // Outflow material\n    \n    // Allocate elements\n    world.elements_static.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic_swap.resize(n_elems);\n    \n    // Initialize all elements with default material and zero energy\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_elems; ++i) {\n        world.elements_static[i].material_idx = DEFAULT_MAT_ID;\n        world.elements_static[i].num_connections = 0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].current_energy = 0.0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].total_flux = 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    // Build connectivity: each element connects to its neighbors in 2D grid\n    for (int x = 0; x < n_elems_root; ++x) {\n        for (int y = 0; y < n_elems_root; ++y) {\n            const int idx = x * n_elems_root + y;\n            ElementStatic& elem = world.elements_static[idx];\n            \n            // Connect to neighbors (up, down, left, right)\n            const int offsets[4][2] = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};\n            \n            for (int n = 0; n < 4; ++n) {\n                const int nx = x + offsets[n][0];\n                const int ny = y + offsets[n][1];\n                \n                // Check if neighbor is within bounds\n                if (nx >= 0 && nx < n_elems_root && ny >= 0 && ny < n_elems_root) {\n                    const int neighbor_idx = nx * n_elems_root + ny;\n                    elem.connected_idx[elem.num_connections] = neighbor_idx;\n                    elem.connected_flux[elem.num_connections] = 1.0;\n                    elem.num_connections++;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Set corner elements as inflow/outflow to create interesting dynamics\n    const int last = n_elems_root - 1;\n    world.elements_static[0 * n_elems_root +    world.elements_static[last * n_elems_root + last].material_idx = INFLOW_MAT_ID;\n}\n\n// Compute energy flux between two elements\ninline val_t computeFlux(const Material& mat, const }\n}\n\n// Validate simulation results\nbool validateResults(const World& world) {\n    val_t energy_sum = 0.0;\n    val_t flux_sum = 0.0;\n    val_t energy_max = {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfyzt5tqQpHguxJfZ5aTz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SFphgQeP3bqLYGyqRQ25XZ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261012-111947/unstructured_claude-haiku-5.5-cc-medium_cuda_r3/unstructured/unstructured.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Types to represent unstructured mesh elements\nusing idx_t = uint64_t;\nusing val_t = double;\n\n// Maximum number of connections per element (for a 2D grid: 4 neighbors)\nconstexpr int MAX_CONNECTIONS = 8;\n\n// Material properties for energy transfer\nstruct Material {\n    val_t transfer_coeff;  // Energy transfer coefficient\n    val_t external_flow;   // External energy source/sink\n};\n\n// Static connectivity information for each element\nstruct ElementStatic {\n    idx_t material_idx;\n    idx_t num_connections;\n    idx_t connected_idx[MAX_CONNECTIONS];     // Indices of connected elements\n    val_t connected_flux[MAX_CONNECTIONS];    // Flux coefficients for each connection\n};\n\n// Dynamic state for each element\nstruct ElementDynamic {\n    val_t current_energy;\n    val_t total_flux;\n};\n\n// World state\nstruct World {\n    std::vector<Material> materials;\n    std::vector<ElementStatic> elements_static;\n    std::vector<ElementDynamic> elements_dynamic;\n    std::vector<ElementDynamic> elements_dynamic_swap;\n};\n\n// Device-side mesh and state. Structure-of-arrays layout so that consecutive\n// threads touch consecutive addresses. Element indices are 32-bit on the device:\n// n_elems_root * n_elems_root is held in an int, so the element count fits.\nstruct DeviceWorld {\n    size_t n_elems = 0;\n    Material* materials = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* material_idx = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* num_connections = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* connected_idx = nullptr;      // [MAX_CONNECTIONS][n_elems], plane-major\n    val_t* connected_flux = nullptr;        // [MAX_CONNECTIONS][n_elems], plane-major\n    val_t* energy[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};  // Ping-pong buffers\n    val_t* flux[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};    // Ping-pong buffers\n};\n\n// Material type IDs\nconstexpr idx_t DEFAULT_MAT_ID = 0;\nconstexpr idx_t INFLOW_MAT_ID = 1;\nconstexpr idx_t OUTFLOW_MAT_ID = 2;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                     \\\n    do {                                                                     \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                           \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                           \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                               \\\n            exit(1);                                                         \\\n        }                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Build a 2D square grid as an unstructured mesh\n// This represents computation on arbitrarily-shaped geometries\nvoid buildSquare2D(World& world, const int n_elems_root) {\n    const int n_elems = n_elems_root * n_elems_root;\n\n    // Initialize materials\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.0});    // Default material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.5});    // Inflow material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, -0.5});   // Outflow material\n\n    // Allocate elements\n    world.elements_static.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic_swap.resize(n_elems);\n\n    // Initialize all elements with default material and zero energy\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_elems; ++i) {\n        world.elements_static[i].material_idx = DEFAULT_MAT_ID;\n        world.elements_static[i].num_connections = 0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].current_energy = 0.0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].total_flux = 0.0;\n    }\n\n    // Build connectivity: each element connects to its neighbors in 2D grid\n    for (int x = 0; x < n_elems_root; ++x) {\n        for (int y = 0; y < n_elems_root; ++y) {\n            const int idx = x * n_elems_root + y;\n            ElementStatic& elem = world.elements_static[idx];\n\n            // Connect to neighbors (up, down, left, right)\n            const int offsets[4][2] = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};\n\n            for (int n = 0; n < 4; ++n) {\n                const int nx = x + offsets[n][0];\n                const int ny = y + offsets[n][1];\n\n                // Check if neighbor is within bounds\n                if (nx >= 0 && nx < n_elems_root && ny >= 0 && ny < n_elems_root) {\n                    const int neighbor_idx = nx * n_elems_root + ny;\n                    elem.connected_idx[elem.num_connections] = neighbor_idx;\n                    elem.connected_flux[elem.num_connections] = 1.0;\n                    elem.num_connections++;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Set corner elements as inflow/outflow to create interesting dynamics\n    const int last = n_elems_root - 1;\n    world.elements_static[0 * n_elems_root + 0].material_idx = INFLOW_MAT_ID;\n    world.elements_static[0 * n_elems_root + last].material_idx = OUTFLOW_MAT_ID;\n    world.elements_static[last * n_elems_root + 0].material_idx = OUTFLOW_MAT_ID;\n    world.elements_static[last * n_elems_root + last].material_idx = INFLOW_MAT_ID;\n}\n\n// Compute energy flux between two elements\n__device__ inline val_t computeFlux(const Material& mat, val_t this_energy,\n                                    val_t connection_flux, val_t other_energy) {\n    return (other_energy - this_energy) * mat.transfer_coeff * connection_flux * 0.25;\n}\n\n// One thread per element: reads the current energies, writes the next state.\n// Floating-point operations run in the same order as the sequential reference.\n__global__ void stepKernel(const DeviceWorld w, const int src) {\n    const size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= w.n_elems) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const int dst = 1 - src;\n    const val_t* energy_in = w.energy[src];\n    const val_t* flux_in = w.flux[src];\n\n    const Material mat = w.materials[w.material_idx[i]];\n    const val_t self_energy = energy_in[i];\n\n    // Start with external flow\n    val_t total_flux = mat.external_flow;\n\n    // Add flux from all connected elements\n    const uint32_t n_conn = w.num_connections[i];\n    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < n_conn; ++j) {\n        const size_t k = static_cast<size_t>(j) * w.n_elems + i;\n        const uint32_t neighbor_idx = w.connected_idx[k];\n        total_flux += computeFlux(mat, self_energy, w.connected_flux[k], energy_in[neighbor_idx]);\n    }\n\n    // Update element state\n    w.energy[dst][i] = self_energy + total_flux;\n    w.flux[dst][i] = flux_in[i] + fabs(total_flux);\n}\n\n// Allocate a device array of `count` elements\ntemplate <typename T>\nT* allocDevice(size_t count) {\n    T* d = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d, count * sizeof(T)));\n    return d;\n}\n\n// Copy a host vector to a new device array\ntemplate <typename T>\nT* toDevice(const std::vector<T>& host) {\n    T* d = allocDevice<T>(host.size());\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d, host.data(), host.size() * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    return d;\n}\n\n// Repack the mesh into device arrays and upload it along with the initial state\nDeviceWorld uploadWorld(const World& world) {\n    DeviceWorld dw;\n    const size_t n = world.elements_static.size();\n    dw.n_elems = n;\n\n    std::vector<uint32_t> material_idx(n);\n    std::vector<uint32_t> num_connections(n);\n    std::vector<uint32_t> connected_idx(MAX_CONNECTIONS * n, 0);\n    std::vector<val_t> connected_flux(MAX_CONNECTIONS * n, 0.0);\n    std::vector<val_t> energy(n);\n    std::vector<val_t> flux(n);\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        const ElementStatic& elem = world.elements_static[i];\n        material_idx[i] = static_cast<uint32_t>(elem.material_idx);\n        num_connections[i] = idx_t INFLOW_MAT_ID = 1;\nconstexpr idx_t OUTFLOW_MAT_ID = 2;\n\n// Build a 2D square grid as an unstructured mesh\n// This represents computation on arbitrarily-shaped geometries\nvoid buildSquare2D(World& world, const int n_elems_root) {\n    const int n_elems = n_elems_root * n_elems_root;\n    \n    // Initialize materials\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.0});    // Default material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, 0.5});    // Inflow material\n    world.materials.emplace_back(Material{0.8, -0.5});   // Outflow material\n    \n    // Allocate elements\n    world.elements_static.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic.resize(n_elems);\n    world.elements_dynamic_swap.resize(n_elems);\n    \n    // Initialize all elements with default material and zero energy\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_elems; ++i) {\n        world.elements_static[i].material_idx = DEFAULT_MAT_ID;\n        world.elements_static[i].num_connections = 0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].current_energy = 0.0;\n        world.elements_dynamic[i].total_flux = 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    // Build connectivity: each element connects to its neighbors in 2D grid\n    for (int x = 0; x < n_elems_root; ++x) {\n        for (int y = 0; y < n_elems_root; ++y) {\n            const int idx = x * n_elems_root + y;\n            ElementStatic& elem = world.elements_static[idx];\n            \n            // Connect to neighbors (up, down, left, right)\n            const int offsets[4][2] = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};\n            \n            for (int n = 0; n < 4; ++n) {\n                const int nx = x + offsets[n][0];\n                const int ny = y + offsets[n][1];\n                \n                // Check if neighbor is within bounds\n                if (nx >= 0 && nx < n_elems_root && ny >= 0 && ny < n_elems_root) {\n                    const int neighbor_idx = nx * n_elems_root + ny;\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfz13n4os3wmSn9Wupzui","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs its simulation on the GPU. Every configuration I tested produces output identical to the original, including the result hash and the `%.17e` sums.\n\n**What changed** (only `unstructured/unstructured.cpp` and `unstructured/CMakeLists.txt`):\n\n- **Kernel:** one thread per element per iteration. Each thread gathers its neighbors' energies and writes the next state into the other buffer. The two buffers ping-pong on the device.\n- **Data layout:** the connectivity is repacked as plane-major structure-of-arrays so neighboring threads read contiguous memory. Indices are 32-bit on the device, which is safe because the element count already has to fit in an `int`.\n- **Timing scope:** upload and download are outside the timed region, matching how the original excluded setup. The timed region is the kernel launches plus a device sync.\n- **Floating point:** the device code keeps the original operation order. nvcc is run with `--fmad=false`, because fused multiply-add changes rounding and would break bit-exactness.\n- **CMake:** the project now enables CUDA, the `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA, and host flags go through `-Xcompiler`. The executable name is unchanged. Architectures default to 80/86/89/90 and can be overridden with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. Minimum CMake went from 3.10 to 3.18.\n- **No CUDA device:** the program exits with an error. There is no CPU fallback, per your requirement.\n\n**Verification**\n- Built with no warnings using nvcc 12.0 and CMake 3.30.\n- Compared against a build of the original across five configurations: default (512² and 10 iterations), 1×1, 2×2 with zero iterations, 37×37 and 100×100. Output matched after removing the timing lines.\n- Negative iteration count matches. The `-h` and unknown-option output match apart from the program path.\n\n**Performance** (RTX 3090, steady state, versus original CPU build)\n\n| Grid, iterations | CPU | GPU |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512², 10 | 22 ms | 0.94 ms |\n| 512², 1000 | 2312 ms | 63 ms |\n| 2048², 100 | 3908 ms | 94 ms |\n\nOne run of the default case took 28.8 ms, which looks like a cold start. The next five runs were all about 0.94 ms.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit**\n- The `Computation time` line now prints milliseconds with three decimals instead of an integer. At GPU speeds the integer value read `0 ms` on small grids and made the rate metrics infinite. The rate lines are computed from the same more precise value.\n- I did not fuse iterations into one kernel or use CUDA graphs. Per-iteration launches are already queued asynchronously, and the kernel is memory-bound, so I judged the extra complexity not worth it. The main remaining cost for very small grids with many iterations would be launch overhead.\n\n**Pre-existing issues I left alone**\n- `-n 0` segfaults both before and after this change. `buildSquare2D` writes out of bounds when the grid size is zero.\n- `output.txt` in the repo has a fresh modification time from this session.
